title: Pleasing God · Chapter 2: The Faith of the God Pleaser
speaker: Joshua Heward-Mills
text:
Chapter 2

# The Faith of the God Pleaser

But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

Hebrews 11:6 (KJV)

There are a particular and specific set of beliefs that a person must have if he will live a life that pleases God. You can have faith in different things, even in Scripture. You can have faith for church growth, marriage, finances, wisdom, or heaven. But there is a particular set of beliefs you must have to please God—whether you're a pastor, church member, usher, or the woman at the well. Whoever you are.

What is faith? It's a firm belief that has its roots exclusively in the Word of God. That's my definition of faith. True faith stands exclusively on God's Word. The only evidence it has to offer is that God said it. There's no empirical evidence, no factual evidence, no information that assists a prediction. Simply because God said it, it's going to be. That's faith.

Without faith it is impossible to please Him. Whatever your place in the church, you need this faith. A pastor needs it. An usher needs it. Every believer needs it. Hebrews 11:6 identifies three convictions: that God exists, that He rewards, and that He rewards those who diligently seek Him.

# 1. You must believe that God exists.

Look at the same Scripture in the English Standard Version:

And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever would draw near to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

Hebrews 11:6 (ESV)

This may sound easy. If I ask a congregation whether God exists, almost everybody will say yes. But the answer of the mouth is not the whole answer.

The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good.

Psalm 14:1 (KJV)

Where has the fool said that there is no God? In the heart. A person can say something different with the mouth while the heart is living as though there is no God.

The verse goes on to describe corruption and abominable works. The life reveals something about what the heart believes. A person who would never publicly deny God can still make decisions as though God does not exist.

For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

Romans 10:10 (KJV)

What is the organ for belief? The heart. What is the organ for confession? The mouth. So you can't use your mouth to believe. We are using our mouths to believe: “I believe in God.” No, no. The mouth is used for confession. It's part of the expression of faith, but it's not what you use to believe. With the heart, man believes.

When I look at the Christians I have dealt with, I am deeply concerned about how many of us live without this heart-level conviction. We say that God exists, yet act as though He neither knows nor sees what we do. What does it really mean to believe in Him?

# a. Believe that He knows everything.

For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.

1 John 3:20 (KJV)

God knows all things. That's the sentence I want you to look at. Those who say they believe in God believe that there is a Being who knows everything.

God knows your thoughts, your intentions. God knows your feelings. God knows what you say behind closed doors. God knows your secrets. God knows those you hate. God knows when you are telling a lie. Do you see why I say most Christians don't believe this? Do you see why, if you believe this, you're likely to live a life that pleases God?

If that conviction settles in your heart, it affects how you live. You cannot comfortably keep a hidden life of pride, lust, or wickedness while assuming that everything is well. There is Someone who knows.

Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful. But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man’s judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self. For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord. Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.

1 Corinthians 4:1-5 (KJV)

With me, Paul says, it's a very small thing—your opinion of me. Very small. Whether you praise or criticise, it's a very tiny thing what you think of me. Many years ago, it became a very small thing. I know and believe in an omniscient God. God knows everything.

That is why we must be careful about passing a final judgment on somebody before the time. The Lord will bring hidden things to light and make the counsels of the heart manifest. There are two matters here: things we do not know about, and the motives behind the things we do know about.

When I look at a man in church, I may describe him as intelligent, gifted, faithful, or called by God. But those are the things I can see. There may be hidden things I know nothing about. My assessment is not complete.

The same applies to your assessment of me. You hear me preach and may think highly of me, but do you know whether I have forgiven everybody who has offended me? Do you know how I spoke to my wife at home? Do you know whether I am obeying the calling God has given me? Those things matter to Him.

As a pastor, I have learned that we do not know everything about a human being. People can pass us without our recognising what is happening. A committed choir member once told me about using an app to arrange sexual encounters. While searching through profiles, the person recognised the church wall in somebody else's photograph. People in the same church could be involved in things that remained hidden from everybody around them.

You don't know. You have no idea. But there's an omniscient Being who knows everything. Who am I hiding from? What do I think I'm doing?

When I was growing up, children in a house across the road did not realise that people could see into the place where they were bathing outside. One day my brother and I called out that we could see them. They immediately ran inside. Becoming aware of somebody's presence changed their behaviour.

That's what God is shouting from heaven: “I can see you. I know.”

The opinions of people, whether complimentary or critical, should not take the place of His judgment. Somebody may praise your ministry or criticise your church. Somebody may admire your preaching or dislike its emphasis. That opinion is not the final verdict on your life.

It would be a poor life to spend all your strength trying to please me. I can only see what a man can see. Find out what the omniscient One thinks of you.

When somebody's wrongdoing becomes known to a pastor, the person may say, “My life is over.” But the act did not suddenly become real when the pastor discovered it. God already knew. The spiritual consequences did not wait for a human being to find out.

We must also be humble when we assess ministers, churches, parents, and people ahead of us. We do not know the full story. Hosea was commanded to marry a woman whose unfaithfulness became part of his painful experience. How would we have judged him if we had known only the appearance of the situation?

The beginning of the word of the LORD by Hosea. And the LORD said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD. So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived, and bare him a son.

Hosea 1:2-3 (KJV)

It is easy to speak confidently about somebody else's life while forgetting that we too will be assessed. A pastor carrying responsibility for many people can make mistakes. A church member can also face difficult things. We need grace and humility, not the confidence of people who imagine they possess all the facts.

When you see a weakness in your parents, put on humility. You may recognise something you should not repeat, but do not assume that you would easily have done better. Let their difficulty lead you to ask God for mercy and grace in your own life.

Think of the family histories of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The complications did not become simpler merely because another generation appeared. Jacob's household included Leah, Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah. Later, Reuben sinned with his father's concubine. These stories should make us careful about self-confident judgment. Knowing somebody else's failure is not proof that we cannot fall.

And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:

Genesis 35:22 (KJV)

The New Living Translation says that He will reveal our private motives:

So don’t make judgments about anyone ahead of time—before the Lord returns. For he will bring our darkest secrets to light and will reveal our private motives. Then God will give to each one whatever praise is due.

1 Corinthians 4:5 (NLT)

You went for evangelism, but why? You gave a big offering, but why? This one is not hidden things. This is what you did that we all saw—but why? You preached a good word, but why? You worked in the church, but why? When she needed money, you gave it to her, but why?

Perhaps you love God and want to do His will. Perhaps you want to be great, to belong to a group, or to be admired. When friends disappoint you, the motive can become visible. If belonging to those friends was the whole reason you came, their offence may become the reason you leave.

Why are you singing in the choir? Why do you come to church? Why do you love this church? Why do you preach? Why do you go on evangelism? People don't live with this knowledge that the Lord knows my motives. He sees all things.

Nothing in all creation is hidden from God. Everything is naked and exposed before his eyes, and he is the one to whom we are accountable.

Hebrews 4:13 (NLT)

Nothing is hidden from Him. We are accountable to Him. This does not remove submission to human leadership. I also have pastors who correct me. They tell me when something in my conduct or speech needs to change. But the reason I must submit is that God has spoken about submission.

Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

Hebrews 13:17 (KJV)

I'm not obeying them because I care about their opinion. I care if God thinks I'm not submitted to them, because God said to obey those who have rule over you. What I want to know is: does God think I've dishonoured them? When I look at the text of Scripture and listen to the voice of the Holy Spirit, do I feel I've made an error? It's more important to be aware of what God thinks than what anybody else thinks.

Consider Miriam and Aaron.

And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman. And they said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

Numbers 12:1-2 (KJV)

They spoke about Moses, but the sentence at the end changes the whole scene: “And the LORD heard it.” Their discussion was not taking place outside God's knowledge. They were not merely comparing themselves with their brother. The Lord was listening.

It is possible for people around you to be pleased while God is displeased. An award, appreciation, or a word of encouragement from a pastor cannot tell you everything about your standing before Him.

Then the Lord said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the leaders of Israel are doing with their idols in dark rooms? They are saying, ‘The Lord doesn’t see us; he has deserted our land!’”

Ezekiel 8:12 (NLT)

The leaders were doing things in the dark and saying that the Lord did not see them. Believing in God must mean more than saying His name. It must include believing that He knows what is happening in the dark rooms of our lives.

# b. Believe that He is everywhere.

Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there.

Psalm 139:7-8 (KJV)

I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

Psalm 16:8 (KJV)

God is everywhere. It's a humbling and a fearful thought. He's not only in church or at Holy Ghost meetings. He's there when we lie, when we steal, when we live in sin. He's present when we abuse our bodies or mistreat our spouses.

He sees a man give generously in church, and He sees whether that same man provides for his household. He sees a woman appear spiritual in public, and He sees her conduct at home. The presence or absence of other people does not alter His presence.

When this becomes real to you, you endeavour to obey in secret as well as in the open. You do not require an audience before you take His Word seriously. The One you want to please is already there.

You cannot comfortably think of Him as far away in heaven, with a visit to Him reserved for Sunday, and expect that thought to produce the same life as a continual awareness of His presence. He is watching when I preach, and He is watching when I go home after preaching.

# c. Believe that He can do anything.

And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

Matthew 28:18 (KJV)

God can do anything. This is deep. God can do anything. When you don't believe God can do anything, you cannot please Him. God has all power. Because I believe this deeply, it helps me to take decisions.

People step into sin because they do not believe that God can provide what they need. Somebody becomes involved in sexual sin because the person does not trust God concerning marriage or a child. Somebody marries for money because the person believes that a wealthy spouse is the only possible source of provision. Somebody steals because the person does not believe that God can provide.

People wrestle and make moves and use connections because they don't believe that it's God who can give them everything they need. So they use human efforts and human attempts to provide or change things.

God can also deal with wrong leadership. David did not need to overthrow Saul. Even when Saul had gone to seek counsel from a witch, God remained able to deal with him. Ahab could be struck by an arrow without God needing us to take control of His position as judge.

So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the LORD, even against the word of the LORD, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it; And enquired not of the LORD: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.

1 Chronicles 10:13-14 (KJV)

And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded. And the battle increased that day: and the king was stayed up in his chariot against the Syrians, and died at even: and the blood ran out of the wound into the midst of the chariot.

1 Kings 22:34-35 (KJV)

God does not need our rebellion or our angry public campaign in order to remain in control. If He wants to remove somebody, He is able. We must not step outside His Word because we think He cannot manage the situation.

The same temptation can arise in marriage. A person becomes impatient and decides to disobey because it seems that God cannot act. But God can change a situation. Our responsibility is not to make sin the solution to a difficulty.

I do not need to lie or alter a receipt to make provision happen. I do not need to force people to give. On one occasion we needed funds for the church windows. The offering we received was far below what was required. Afterwards, somebody contacted me to say that God had prompted a gift that would meet the need. We were able to pay for the windows. God did not require me to manipulate the congregation.

I have known God as my source when I preached without a salary, when I did not have money for marriage, and when my wife and I did not have enough to buy a bed. I have had to know Him as my source in loneliness and when people lifted their hands against me.

But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.

Matthew 5:39-41 (KJV)

Jesus' instructions about the other cheek and the second mile require confidence in God. If I believe I must personally repay every wrong, I will struggle to obey them. But I can leave the matter with the One who has power to deal with it.

Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord. Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

Romans 12:19-21 (KJV)

“Vengeance is Mine. I will repay.” Put your hand down. He said He will pay, and you want to pay for yourself? No, no. Let God deal with it. You sow a seed; you reap what you have sown. Leave things to God.

Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

Galatians 6:7 (KJV)

Peter told Ananias that his deception had reached beyond men to God. It is a serious thing to imagine that getting past a human being settles the matter.

But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land? Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.

Acts 5:3-4 (KJV)

Abraham's two sons also illustrate the difference between human effort and the fulfilment of God's promise.

The Scriptures say that Abraham had two sons, one from his slave wife and one from his freeborn wife. The son of the slave wife was born in a human attempt to bring about the fulfillment of God’s promise. But the son of the freeborn wife was born as God’s own fulfillment of his promise.

Galatians 4:22-23 (NLT)

God promised a son. The attempt to make that promise happen through Hagar was a human arrangement. Isaac came according to the promise. We must allow God to fulfil what He has said instead of stepping into disobedience to help Him.

And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

Genesis 12:2-3 (KJV)

If God has said that He will bless you or make your name great, you do not need to make fame your private project. Examine the motive behind even religious activity. We may call something spreading the Word while secretly trying to make ourselves known.

I have often tried to move away from the things that would make me appear important. I am not naturally eager for live streaming or releasing messages. I want the motive of my heart to remain before God. What finally matters is whether He is behind what I am doing.

After you have done His will, you need patience.

For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.

Hebrews 10:36 (KJV)

He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.

Ecclesiastes 3:11 (KJV)

He works in His time, not according to our clock. Allow Him to take you through the difficult part. Do not throw away obedience because you want the outcome immediately.

For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.

Romans 8:18 (KJV)

This is my ethos. This is my compass, my engine. This has guided me these years of my life. This is what I think, what I know, what I believe. These are my convictions. This is what moves me. God is in control. Follow God. Obey His Word. Do what He says. In His time, He makes things beautiful. Trust God. Allow God.

When people applaud a sermon, I hope there is also approval in heaven. I hope I have said what God wanted me to say. Sometimes obedience means risking the displeasure of people. Their approval cannot become more important than His.

For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

Galatians 1:10 (KJV)

# 2. You must believe that He is a rewarder.

Why must you believe that God is a rewarder? Or you'll ask yourself the question most of you ask all the time: “For what?” Submit—for what? Love your wife—for what? Stay there—for what? Take the blame for what is not your fault—for what? Because He's a rewarder. There's a reward at the end.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.

Hebrews 12:1-2 (KJV)

Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before Him. There was something beyond the suffering. In the same way, knowing that God rewards gives us strength to endure.

There's a reward for humility. Many times I've taken the humble road. There's a reward for forgiveness. Oh yes. If you're a leader, forgiveness is one of your secrets to maintaining authority. People who forgive are fearful. When you come and say, “Don't worry, it's fine. I forgive you for lying to me,” there's something about it.

But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.

Psalm 130:4 (KJV)

People become tired when they no longer believe that serving God leads anywhere. Think of a student enduring the demands of a course because there is a degree at the end. The expectation of a result helps the student continue through the difficult years.

There is a blessing in following God's voice.

And they thirsted not when he led them through the deserts: he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them: he clave the rock also, and the waters gushed out.

Isaiah 48:21 (KJV)

They did not thirst while He led them through the deserts. Following Him does not mean that you must first remove every desert from the journey. There is provision in His leading.

There is a reward for restraining an unkind word, even when you think the description is true. Not everything we could say is something we should say. Obedience concerns our words as well as our actions.

There is also a reward for giving. I am not saying that a person must tithe in order to become a Christian. But neither should we pretend that giving to God is of no consequence and has no blessing attached to it. Believe that He is a rewarder.

# 3. You must believe that diligently seeking Him will be rewarded.

Those who do not believe this struggle to continue through dry and difficult times in prayer. They slowly drift away because they do not believe that the search will lead to anything.

The reward for seeking the Lord is the Lord Himself. You'll be rewarded with the person of the Holy Spirit when you seek Him daily. Those who seek Him diligently will find Him.

There is a phrase in Proverbs that expresses the diligence of a search: “diligently to seek thy face.”

Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.

Proverbs 7:15 (KJV)

Those words occur in a human encounter, but consider the earnestness of seeking until the person sought is found. Do you believe that seeking God will lead to finding Him? Do you believe that the time spent praying, waiting, reading the Bible, and pursuing Him has a reward?

That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:

Acts 17:27 (KJV)

God wants to be sought. He is not far from us, yet He desires that we reach after Him. After years of following the Lord, this is something I have come to see: Jesus longs to be longed for.

Do not give up on the search because a season feels dry. Diligently seek His voice and His presence. He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him.

# 4. Let this faith govern the choices you make.

Even giving is an opportunity to express this faith. Another person may not know what is in your hand, but God knows. What you give is before Him. The size of somebody else's impression is not the deciding matter.

Yield to His will. Stop assuming that you must always choose the thing you have already decided is best for you.

I knew of somebody who had made a decision that proved costly. Later, I heard about another decision the person was preparing to make. As I looked into it, I realised that it was leading in the same direction, and perhaps further. The person thought this time was different. But the problem had not merely been the particular choice. The problem was the insistence on choosing in the same way—having to get one's own way.

Settle your heart before God. Be ready for what He has for you. In the summer of 2013, I settled my own heart concerning marriage: whatever God had for me, I was ready to receive it.

If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.

John 7:17 (KJV)

Willingness matters. You may be outwardly doing something while inwardly resisting it. Let your desire become the desire to do His will. That willingness prepares you to receive His teaching and guidance.

Do not let a list of preferred appearances rule the search for a spouse. How something looks is not always what it is. Be willing for God to lead you, even when the way does not resemble what you had pictured.

For somebody in a troubled courtship, taking warning signs seriously may mean ending that relationship rather than proceeding into marriage. Marriage is a different commitment. Do not let greed or covetousness persuade you to abandon your obligations. Keep seeking God and doing what His Word requires.

Yea, they spake against God; they said, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?

Psalm 78:19 (KJV)

God can furnish a table in the wilderness. Do not make another human being your final source. He can provide where you cannot see how provision will come.

Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

Psalm 23:5 (KJV)

The table can be prepared in the presence of opposition. The other person does not have to disappear before God can give you peace and provision. Keep your trust in Him.

Young men also need humility in seeking guidance. The Word speaks to young men about strength and the Word of God abiding in them.

I have written unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one.

1 John 2:14 (KJV)

But strength is not a substitute for meekness.

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way.

Psalm 25:9 (KJV)

Sometimes the problem is not that a person has heard guidance and disobeyed it. Pride has made the person unwilling to receive guidance at all. Be humble enough to be led. Do not assume that a humble-looking choice must be beneath you.

A woman close to me once reflected on an earlier relationship and said that, without the things she had gone through, she would not have married her husband or appreciated him as she now did. I agreed. Some experiences help us receive what pride would once have rejected.

# 5. Guard against the surprising foundations of pride.

These are surprising foundations of pride—things you wouldn't think would make you proud. A little brightness, beauty, wisdom, riches, prayer, fasting, revelation. We have to be humble.

# a. A sense of perfection.

Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God; thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire. Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee.

Ezekiel 28:14-15 (KJV)

Some people become proud because they have not made the mistakes others have made. They have not smoked, slept with anybody, or been caught in some scandal. But the absence of a known failure is no reason to exalt yourself. The passage speaks of perfection until iniquity was found. You need humility, not confidence that there is nothing wrong with you.

# b. Beauty.

Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.

Ezekiel 28:17 (KJV)

Beauty can lift up a heart. A handsome man or a beautiful woman has a temptation to pride. This does not mean that humble people are unattractive; it means that an admired appearance needs to be held humbly.

# c. Wisdom.

The same verse speaks of corrupted wisdom. Being wise does not remove the need for humility. Wisdom itself can become something in which a person glories.

# d. Brightness.

When somebody begins to shine, pride can enter quickly. A young person leads worship and people are moved. A musician plays and the presence of God is sensed. Somebody shares a quiet time and people are blessed. A little brightness can become a great temptation if the heart is not guarded.

# e. Riches.

By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches:

Ezekiel 28:5 (KJV)

Prosperity can lift the heart. What has increased in your hands must not become an increase of pride within you.

# f. Prayer and fasting.

Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican. The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

Luke 18:10-14 (KJV)

The Pharisee listed his religious practices while exalting himself above other people. The publican could hardly lift his eyes to heaven and asked for mercy. It was the publican who went home justified. Prayer, fasting, and giving must not become a platform for looking down on others.

# g. Revelation.

And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.

2 Corinthians 12:7 (KJV)

Paul spoke of a thorn in the flesh lest the abundance of revelation should exalt him above measure. Even spiritual insight can become a temptation to pride.

I have found that some of the highest moments in my ministry have been accompanied by painful personal experiences. When I remember major conferences or my consecration, I also remember difficult things I was going through at the time. Great outward moments do not mean that everything in a person's private life is easy. God knows how to deal with us and keep our hearts before Him.

Believe that He knows. Believe that He is present. Believe that He can act. Believe that He rewards, and keep seeking Him diligently. This is the faith of the God pleaser.
